content: Tetracycline is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including acne. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication should be taken on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after meals, as directed by your doctor, typically two to four times daily. If stomach upset occurs, consult your doctor about taking it with food. Each dose should be taken with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters), unless otherwise instructed. Avoid lying down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medication. Tetracycline should not be taken alongside products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate (e.g., antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products like milk or yogurt, or calcium-enriched juice) within two to three hours before or after taking the medication. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, mouth sores, a black hairy tongue, sore throat, dizziness, headache, or rectal discomfort. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. If IH develops, it typically resolves after stopping the medication, but there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. Tetracycline may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of tetracycline may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection (oral or vaginal fungal infection). Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This medication should not be used in children under 8 years of age, as it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as tetracycline can harm an unborn baby and passes into breast milk. You should not become pregnant while using this medication. This drug may also interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine) and certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist to avoid potential drug interactions. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, as taking outdated tetracycline can cause serious illness. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only and should not be used for other infections unless directed by your doctor. Keep all medical and lab appointments while taking this medication. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about tetracycline. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
